history.period: Border trading town; Indo-Myanmar border trade point established 2004
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. 'Zokhawthar' is not a temple name; it is the India-Myanmar border trading town in Champhai district, Mizoram (population 2,632 in 2011), about 28-29 km east of Champhai town on the Tiau river opposite Rihkhawdar (Rih) village in Myanmar. The Zokhawthar-Rih border trade point, India's second Indo-Myanmar border trade post, was established here in 2004, and Zokhawthar was later designated an authorised land immigration check-post (the second in Mizoram after Zorinpui). No Hindu temple in or named after Zokhawthar appears in any published source; web searches return only the border market, trade/immigration references, and churches (e.g. Mizoram Methodist Kohhran). CSV correction: the CSV's town column reads 'Champhai' (which is the district name); corrected here to town 'Zokhawthar', district 'Champhai'.

name: Zokhawthar
town_description: Zokhawthar is a border town in Champhai district, Mizoram, on the India-Myanmar border, about 28 km east of Champhai town across the Tiau river from Rihkhawdar (Rih) in Myanmar's Chin State. Designated as the Zokhawthar-Rih Indo-Myanmar border trade point in 2004 and later as an authorised immigration check-post, it is one of Mizoram's largest trading centres after Aizawl, with a daily border market selling Myanmar imports and local goods. Indian nationals from other states need an Inner Line Permit (ILP) to visit Mizoram, including Zokhawthar.

travel.airport: Lengpui Airport (Aizawl); the state capital is about 228 km from the Zokhawthar zero point per Mizoram customs documentation (verify).
travel.railway: No railway station nearby (verify); nearest railheads are in Assam.
travel.road: Approx. 28-29 km east of Champhai town by road; regular taxis, shared sumos and buses ply between Aizawl, Champhai and Zokhawthar (verify current schedule).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for Mizoram hill weather (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Border market: 7:00 AM-4:00 PM daily per travelsetu (verify on arrival). No temple exists, so no temple hours apply.
